While acknowledging concerns about the distribution of benefits, he maintained that the surveillance contract had positively affected many communities. “The truth is that many communities and youths have benefited from the surveillance contract. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. “It represents a strategic recalibration of Nigeria’s energy ambitions at a time when global markets are shifting rapidly, and the country faces pressure to strengthen production, attract capital, and reposition itself in the era of energy transition. “As NUPRC is looking forward to harvesting an additional 500 million barrels to the national crude oil reserve from the 2025 bid round, these extra barrels are expected to be driven by the commencement of operational activities of the 31 companies that emerged as winners of 37 oil and gas blocks in the bid round licensing. Protection of oil assets should also form part of the priority areas for stakeholders, and that is where TSSNL should always be supported to achieve its goals,” he said. Martins explained that the awarded assets span several producing and frontier basins, including 16 Niger Delta Onshore blocks, 18 Niger Delta Shallow Water blocks, one Niger Delta Deep Offshore block, three Benin Basin Onshore blocks, four Anambra Basin Onshore blocks, four Chad Basin Onshore blocks and four Benue Trough blocks. The Chief Executive Officer, NUPRC, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, said at the Commercial Bid Conference for the Nigeria Licensing Round, themed “Expanding Opportunities: Right Play, Right Place, Right Time”, that the assets on offer have significant reserve potential. “The assets available in this licensing round have potential to add about 500 million barrels to Nigeria’s reserves, increasing our existing reserves of crude oil and condensate—which currently stand at 37.01 billion barrels—and 215.19 trillion cubic feet of gas,” she said. Eyesan said the absence of bids for the 13 frontier blocks was not unexpected. According to her, the assets presented during the 2025 commercial bid had previously been recovered from operators, while the commission would continue assessing other assets for possible inclusion in future licensing exercises. “The reason why we are in the market is because of the blocks that we have recovered from existing operators,” she said. Industry analysts also noted that the licensing round attracted notable investor interest in frontier basins. Some winners The companies that emerged as winners of the 2025 Licensing Round include SSonic Petroleum Limited (PPL 2A29), CFP Pipeline and Flowlines (2A30), Dutchford E&P Limited (2A32), Attabanson Global Company Limited (2A33 and PPL 901), Rosem Energy Limited (2A38), and Pivot-GIS Limited (2A39). The others include Network E&P (2A40), Asharami (2A41), LexOil (2A42), BVOF (2A43), GupscoEnergy Limited (2A44 and 2A51), Saratoga (2A45), Volante (2A46), Concept-Reel Petroleum Services Limited (2A47 and 2A55), Clinton Oil Field (2A48 and 2A62), Nuway Oaklane Limited (2A49), Ramec (2A50), Italia (2A53), Blueridge E&P (2A54), Up Energies Limited (2A56), and AYM Shafa (2A57). There are also Blackrock Holdings Limited (2A58), Funtay Integrated Business Limited (2A59), Riparian Development and Production Limited (2A60), Nikstallis (2A61 and PPL 900), Stardeep Petroleum (PPL 2010), Dakoda & U Limited (PPL 308 and PPL 800), Southborne Oil and Gas Limited (PPL 902), Lanaka Petroleum (PPL 903), Highban Resources Limited (PPL 700) and Eyre Energy Limited (PPL 801). Views from stakeholders Stakeholders have continued to emphasise the importance of pipeline protection to Nigeria’s oil production ambitions, arguing that safeguarding critical infrastructure remains essential to sustaining output, attracting investment and supporting broader economic growth. Related News Over 1,100 host community projects ongoing in Niger Delta, says NUPRC Oil block bidding: Inside Nigeria’s seven-hour transparency test REAN urges action to accelerate Nigeria’s clean energy transition In a published report, the President-General of the Niger Delta Progressive Alliance, Nse Udoh, argued that pipeline surveillance has helped national institutions move from reactive crisis management to more strategic planning and long-term decision-making. “It is important to clarify the role of pipeline surveillance within the wider energy landscape. Energy security encompasses the full value chain, from exploration and production to refining, distribution, pricing policy, and subsidy frameworks. Pipeline surveillance does not manage these domains,” he said. Udoh, however, maintained that pipeline surveillance plays a critical supporting role by protecting infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. “Its mandate is precise: safeguarding critical infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. Yet this single function has proven foundational. Without secure transportation channels, production targets falter, refining plans collapse, exports decline, and fiscal projections become unreliable,” he added. He further argued that asset protection underpins the efficient operation of the petroleum value chain. “Asset protection, in this context, is not a supporting activity. It is a precondition for economic order. In effect, the pipeline is the hinge on which the entire petroleum value chain turns. When that hinge is weak, every other link in the chain carries strain. When it is secure, the entire system gains coherence,” he wrote. According to him, sustained monitoring and rapid-response measures have contributed to fewer pipeline breaches and incidents of illegal tapping, while improvements in production have helped strengthen Nigeria’s position in the international oil market. Udoh also argued that greater certainty in crude oil transportation supports planning across the petroleum value chain. “Economic stability follows predictability. When crude flows are secure, refineries can plan feedstock intake with assurance. Export commitments can be met without fear of sudden shortfalls. Gas-to-power projects can operate without recurrent shutdown risks. “Investors can assess Nigeria’s petroleum sector with clearer risk profiles. Surveillance therefore does more than stop theft. It reintroduces reliability into national energy planning. And reliability is the bedrock upon which sustainable economic growth is built. “With predictable flows, national budgeting becomes more credible, infrastructure planning becomes more precise, and long-term contracts become easier to negotiate. Predictability is the silent currency of modern economies, and pipeline surveillance has begun restoring it,” he stated. He added that improved production accountability has supported export earnings, strengthened foreign exchange inflows and enhanced fiscal capacity, while helping national oil company operations become more efficient through lower losses and improved operational continuity. According to Udoh, more stable revenues also improve government planning by creating greater fiscal certainty and supporting investment in infrastructure, social services and economic diversification. Traditional rulers and community leaders in the Niger Delta have also called for continued support for Tantita Security Services Limited following a vote of confidence passed on the company by the National Assembly. The leaders said the company’s involvement in protecting oil and gas pipelines had coincided with improvements in security across some oil-producing communities, while also creating employment opportunities for young people. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. “The assets available in this licensing round have potential to add about 500 million barrels to Nigeria’s reserves, increasing our existing reserves of crude oil and condensate—which currently stand at 37.01 billion barrels—and 215.19 trillion cubic feet of gas,” she said. Eyesan said the absence of bids for the 13 frontier blocks was not unexpected. According to her, the assets presented during the 2025 commercial bid had previously been recovered from operators, while the commission would continue assessing other assets for possible inclusion in future licensing exercises. “The reason why we are in the market is because of the blocks that we have recovered from existing operators,” she said. Industry analysts also noted that the licensing round attracted notable investor interest in frontier basins. Some winners The companies that emerged as winners of the 2025 Licensing Round include SSonic Petroleum Limited (PPL 2A29), CFP Pipeline and Flowlines (2A30), Dutchford E&P Limited (2A32), Attabanson Global Company Limited (2A33 and PPL 901), Rosem Energy Limited (2A38), and Pivot-GIS Limited (2A39). The others include Network E&P (2A40), Asharami (2A41), LexOil (2A42), BVOF (2A43), GupscoEnergy Limited (2A44 and 2A51), Saratoga (2A45), Volante (2A46), Concept-Reel Petroleum Services Limited (2A47 and 2A55), Clinton Oil Field (2A48 and 2A62), Nuway Oaklane Limited (2A49), Ramec (2A50), Italia (2A53), Blueridge E&P (2A54), Up Energies Limited (2A56), and AYM Shafa (2A57). There are also Blackrock Holdings Limited (2A58), Funtay Integrated Business Limited (2A59), Riparian Development and Production Limited (2A60), Nikstallis (2A61 and PPL 900), Stardeep Petroleum (PPL 2010), Dakoda & U Limited (PPL 308 and PPL 800), Southborne Oil and Gas Limited (PPL 902), Lanaka Petroleum (PPL 903), Highban Resources Limited (PPL 700) and Eyre Energy Limited (PPL 801). Views from stakeholders Stakeholders have continued to emphasise the importance of pipeline protection to Nigeria’s oil production ambitions, arguing that safeguarding critical infrastructure remains essential to sustaining output, attracting investment and supporting broader economic growth. Related News Over 1,100 host community projects ongoing in Niger Delta, says NUPRC Oil block bidding: Inside Nigeria’s seven-hour transparency test REAN urges action to accelerate Nigeria’s clean energy transition In a published report, the President-General of the Niger Delta Progressive Alliance, Nse Udoh, argued that pipeline surveillance has helped national institutions move from reactive crisis management to more strategic planning and long-term decision-making. “It is important to clarify the role of pipeline surveillance within the wider energy landscape. Energy security encompasses the full value chain, from exploration and production to refining, distribution, pricing policy, and subsidy frameworks. Pipeline surveillance does not manage these domains,” he said. Udoh, however, maintained that pipeline surveillance plays a critical supporting role by protecting infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. “Its mandate is precise: safeguarding critical infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. Yet this single function has proven foundational. Without secure transportation channels, production targets falter, refining plans collapse, exports decline, and fiscal projections become unreliable,” he added. He further argued that asset protection underpins the efficient operation of the petroleum value chain. “Asset protection, in this context, is not a supporting activity. It is a precondition for economic order. In effect, the pipeline is the hinge on which the entire petroleum value chain turns. When that hinge is weak, every other link in the chain carries strain. When it is secure, the entire system gains coherence,” he wrote. According to him, sustained monitoring and rapid-response measures have contributed to fewer pipeline breaches and incidents of illegal tapping, while improvements in production have helped strengthen Nigeria’s position in the international oil market. Udoh also argued that greater certainty in crude oil transportation supports planning across the petroleum value chain. “Economic stability follows predictability. When crude flows are secure, refineries can plan feedstock intake with assurance. Export commitments can be met without fear of sudden shortfalls. Gas-to-power projects can operate without recurrent shutdown risks. “Investors can assess Nigeria’s petroleum sector with clearer risk profiles. Surveillance therefore does more than stop theft. It reintroduces reliability into national energy planning. And reliability is the bedrock upon which sustainable economic growth is built. “With predictable flows, national budgeting becomes more credible, infrastructure planning becomes more precise, and long-term contracts become easier to negotiate. Predictability is the silent currency of modern economies, and pipeline surveillance has begun restoring it,” he stated. He added that improved production accountability has supported export earnings, strengthened foreign exchange inflows and enhanced fiscal capacity, while helping national oil company operations become more efficient through lower losses and improved operational continuity. According to Udoh, more stable revenues also improve government planning by creating greater fiscal certainty and supporting investment in infrastructure, social services and economic diversification. Traditional rulers and community leaders in the Niger Delta have also called for continued support for Tantita Security Services Limited following a vote of confidence passed on the company by the National Assembly. The leaders said the company’s involvement in protecting oil and gas pipelines had coincided with improvements in security across some oil-producing communities, while also creating employment opportunities for young people. Commenting on the development, the President-General of the Isoko Development Union, Christopher Akpotu, commended the joint committee of the Senate and House of Representatives for dismissing petitions filed against the company. He described the decision as beneficial to the Niger Delta and urged stakeholders to focus on expanding opportunities in the oil and gas sector rather than internal disputes. “That is the right way to go,” he said. “There are many opportunities in the oil and gas sector. We should focus on how to derive more benefits rather than fighting over what has already been allocated.” Akpotu cautioned that prolonged disagreements among host communities could create opportunities for outsiders to benefit at their expense. “At the end of the day, if we continue fighting, we give room to those who have no stake in our communities to take what rightfully belongs to us,” he added. While acknowledging concerns about the distribution of benefits, he maintained that the surveillance contract had positively affected many communities. “The truth is that many communities and youths have benefited from the surveillance contract. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. The companies that emerged as winners of the 2025 Licensing Round include SSonic Petroleum Limited (PPL 2A29), CFP Pipeline and Flowlines (2A30), Dutchford E&P Limited (2A32), Attabanson Global Company Limited (2A33 and PPL 901), Rosem Energy Limited (2A38), and Pivot-GIS Limited (2A39). The others include Network E&P (2A40), Asharami (2A41), LexOil (2A42), BVOF (2A43), GupscoEnergy Limited (2A44 and 2A51), Saratoga (2A45), Volante (2A46), Concept-Reel Petroleum Services Limited (2A47 and 2A55), Clinton Oil Field (2A48 and 2A62), Nuway Oaklane Limited (2A49), Ramec (2A50), Italia (2A53), Blueridge E&P (2A54), Up Energies Limited (2A56), and AYM Shafa (2A57). There are also Blackrock Holdings Limited (2A58), Funtay Integrated Business Limited (2A59), Riparian Development and Production Limited (2A60), Nikstallis (2A61 and PPL 900), Stardeep Petroleum (PPL 2010), Dakoda & U Limited (PPL 308 and PPL 800), Southborne Oil and Gas Limited (PPL 902), Lanaka Petroleum (PPL 903), Highban Resources Limited (PPL 700) and Eyre Energy Limited (PPL 801). Views from stakeholders Stakeholders have continued to emphasise the importance of pipeline protection to Nigeria’s oil production ambitions, arguing that safeguarding critical infrastructure remains essential to sustaining output, attracting investment and supporting broader economic growth. Related News Over 1,100 host community projects ongoing in Niger Delta, says NUPRC Oil block bidding: Inside Nigeria’s seven-hour transparency test REAN urges action to accelerate Nigeria’s clean energy transition In a published report, the President-General of the Niger Delta Progressive Alliance, Nse Udoh, argued that pipeline surveillance has helped national institutions move from reactive crisis management to more strategic planning and long-term decision-making. “It is important to clarify the role of pipeline surveillance within the wider energy landscape. Energy security encompasses the full value chain, from exploration and production to refining, distribution, pricing policy, and subsidy frameworks. Pipeline surveillance does not manage these domains,” he said. Udoh, however, maintained that pipeline surveillance plays a critical supporting role by protecting infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. “Its mandate is precise: safeguarding critical infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. Yet this single function has proven foundational. Without secure transportation channels, production targets falter, refining plans collapse, exports decline, and fiscal projections become unreliable,” he added. He further argued that asset protection underpins the efficient operation of the petroleum value chain. “Asset protection, in this context, is not a supporting activity. It is a precondition for economic order. In effect, the pipeline is the hinge on which the entire petroleum value chain turns. When that hinge is weak, every other link in the chain carries strain. When it is secure, the entire system gains coherence,” he wrote. According to him, sustained monitoring and rapid-response measures have contributed to fewer pipeline breaches and incidents of illegal tapping, while improvements in production have helped strengthen Nigeria’s position in the international oil market. Udoh also argued that greater certainty in crude oil transportation supports planning across the petroleum value chain. “Economic stability follows predictability. When crude flows are secure, refineries can plan feedstock intake with assurance. Export commitments can be met without fear of sudden shortfalls. Gas-to-power projects can operate without recurrent shutdown risks. “Investors can assess Nigeria’s petroleum sector with clearer risk profiles. Surveillance therefore does more than stop theft. It reintroduces reliability into national energy planning. And reliability is the bedrock upon which sustainable economic growth is built. “With predictable flows, national budgeting becomes more credible, infrastructure planning becomes more precise, and long-term contracts become easier to negotiate. Predictability is the silent currency of modern economies, and pipeline surveillance has begun restoring it,” he stated. He added that improved production accountability has supported export earnings, strengthened foreign exchange inflows and enhanced fiscal capacity, while helping national oil company operations become more efficient through lower losses and improved operational continuity. According to Udoh, more stable revenues also improve government planning by creating greater fiscal certainty and supporting investment in infrastructure, social services and economic diversification. Traditional rulers and community leaders in the Niger Delta have also called for continued support for Tantita Security Services Limited following a vote of confidence passed on the company by the National Assembly. The leaders said the company’s involvement in protecting oil and gas pipelines had coincided with improvements in security across some oil-producing communities, while also creating employment opportunities for young people. Commenting on the development, the President-General of the Isoko Development Union, Christopher Akpotu, commended the joint committee of the Senate and House of Representatives for dismissing petitions filed against the company. He described the decision as beneficial to the Niger Delta and urged stakeholders to focus on expanding opportunities in the oil and gas sector rather than internal disputes. “That is the right way to go,” he said. “There are many opportunities in the oil and gas sector. We should focus on how to derive more benefits rather than fighting over what has already been allocated.” Akpotu cautioned that prolonged disagreements among host communities could create opportunities for outsiders to benefit at their expense. “At the end of the day, if we continue fighting, we give room to those who have no stake in our communities to take what rightfully belongs to us,” he added. While acknowledging concerns about the distribution of benefits, he maintained that the surveillance contract had positively affected many communities. “The truth is that many communities and youths have benefited from the surveillance contract. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. He described the decision as beneficial to the Niger Delta and urged stakeholders to focus on expanding opportunities in the oil and gas sector rather than internal disputes. “That is the right way to go,” he said. “There are many opportunities in the oil and gas sector. We should focus on how to derive more benefits rather than fighting over what has already been allocated.” Akpotu cautioned that prolonged disagreements among host communities could create opportunities for outsiders to benefit at their expense. “At the end of the day, if we continue fighting, we give room to those who have no stake in our communities to take what rightfully belongs to us,” he added. While acknowledging concerns about the distribution of benefits, he maintained that the surveillance contract had positively affected many communities. “The truth is that many communities and youths have benefited from the surveillance contract. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. In a published report, the President-General of the Niger Delta Progressive Alliance, Nse Udoh, argued that pipeline surveillance has helped national institutions move from reactive crisis management to more strategic planning and long-term decision-making. “It is important to clarify the role of pipeline surveillance within the wider energy landscape. Energy security encompasses the full value chain, from exploration and production to refining, distribution, pricing policy, and subsidy frameworks. Pipeline surveillance does not manage these domains,” he said. Udoh, however, maintained that pipeline surveillance plays a critical supporting role by protecting infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. “Its mandate is precise: safeguarding critical infrastructure that transports petroleum resources. Yet this single function has proven foundational. Without secure transportation channels, production targets falter, refining plans collapse, exports decline, and fiscal projections become unreliable,” he added. He further argued that asset protection underpins the efficient operation of the petroleum value chain. “Asset protection, in this context, is not a supporting activity. It is a precondition for economic order. In effect, the pipeline is the hinge on which the entire petroleum value chain turns. When that hinge is weak, every other link in the chain carries strain. When it is secure, the entire system gains coherence,” he wrote. According to him, sustained monitoring and rapid-response measures have contributed to fewer pipeline breaches and incidents of illegal tapping, while improvements in production have helped strengthen Nigeria’s position in the international oil market. Udoh also argued that greater certainty in crude oil transportation supports planning across the petroleum value chain. “Economic stability follows predictability. When crude flows are secure, refineries can plan feedstock intake with assurance. Export commitments can be met without fear of sudden shortfalls. Gas-to-power projects can operate without recurrent shutdown risks. “Investors can assess Nigeria’s petroleum sector with clearer risk profiles. Surveillance therefore does more than stop theft. It reintroduces reliability into national energy planning. And reliability is the bedrock upon which sustainable economic growth is built. “With predictable flows, national budgeting becomes more credible, infrastructure planning becomes more precise, and long-term contracts become easier to negotiate. Predictability is the silent currency of modern economies, and pipeline surveillance has begun restoring it,” he stated. He added that improved production accountability has supported export earnings, strengthened foreign exchange inflows and enhanced fiscal capacity, while helping national oil company operations become more efficient through lower losses and improved operational continuity. According to Udoh, more stable revenues also improve government planning by creating greater fiscal certainty and supporting investment in infrastructure, social services and economic diversification. Traditional rulers and community leaders in the Niger Delta have also called for continued support for Tantita Security Services Limited following a vote of confidence passed on the company by the National Assembly. While acknowledging concerns about the distribution of benefits, he maintained that the surveillance contract had positively affected many communities. “The truth is that many communities and youths have benefited from the surveillance contract. It may not be evenly distributed, but the impact is evident,” he said. He also urged Tantita to broaden engagement with traditional rulers, youths and community leaders to promote fairness and strengthen long-term cooperation. Similarly, the President-General of the Ughelli Descendants Union, Sam Akpemegi, said security had improved since the company began operations, noting that both physical surveillance and intelligence-driven strategies had been deployed. “They have done very well and improved security since they began operations,” he said, adding that the company’s activities now extend across many communities. Akpemegi added that the company’s presence had benefited both traditional institutions and local residents, while calling for continued support for its operations. In the same vein, the Odiologbo of Ofagbe Kingdom, Ogaga Ikpoku, backed the National Assembly’s decision, describing it as timely and beneficial to peace and stability in the region. Stakeholders also argued that improved protection of oil assets has produced environmental and social benefits in parts of the Niger Delta. They noted that illegal refining and pipeline sabotage had previously polluted waterways, degraded farmlands and exposed communities to environmental and security risks, adding that sustained surveillance efforts against illegal refining sites and repeated pipeline breaches have supported ongoing environmental recovery. “Economic stability follows predictability. When crude flows are secure, refineries can plan feedstock intake with assurance. Export commitments can be met without fear of sudden shortfalls. Gas-to-power projects can operate without recurrent shutdown risks. “Investors can assess Nigeria’s petroleum sector with clearer risk profiles. Surveillance therefore does more than stop theft. It reintroduces reliability into national energy planning. And reliability is the bedrock upon which sustainable economic growth is built. “With predictable flows, national budgeting becomes more credible, infrastructure planning becomes more precise, and long-term contracts become easier to negotiate. Predictability is the silent currency of modern economies, and pipeline surveillance has begun restoring it,” he stated. He added that improved production accountability has supported export earnings, strengthened foreign exchange inflows and enhanced fiscal capacity, while helping national oil company operations become more efficient through lower losses and improved operational continuity. According to Udoh, more stable revenues also improve government planning by creating greater fiscal certainty and supporting investment in infrastructure, social services and economic diversification. Traditional rulers and community leaders in the Niger Delta have also called for continued support for Tantita Security Services Limited following a vote of confidence passed on the company by the National Assembly. The leaders said the company’s involvement in protecting oil and gas pipelines had coincided with improvements in security across some oil-producing communities, while also creating employment opportunities for young people. Title: NVIDIA Expands NVIDIA Agent Toolkit With NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and CUDA-X Libraries to Transform How the World Engineers, Designs and Builds
URL: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/27/3333237/0/en/NVIDIA-Expands-NVIDIA-Agent-Toolkit-With-NVIDIA-PhysicsNeMo-and-CUDA-X-Libraries-to-Transform-How-the-World-Engineers-Designs-and-Builds.html
Time Published: 2026-07-27T00:45:00Z
Full Content:
July 26, 2026 20:45 ET | Source: NVIDIA NVIDIA News Summary: LONG BEACH, Calif., July 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NVIDIA today announced an expansion of NVIDIA Agent Toolkit for engineering, now adding NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo™ and CUDA-X™ libraries as agent-ready tools and skills built to transform how the world designs and develops products. Building the next generation of chips and systems requires teams to connect physics, simulation and performance analysis across increasingly complex design cycles. A new class of autonomous AI engineers is emerging to help take on that complexity — using specialized tools, running simulations and generating high-fidelity data to help scale chip design, verification, packaging and systems. Now included in NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA has re-architected PhysicsNeMo into a set of agent-friendly libraries and added new and updated CUDA-X libraries to support complex engineering work. PhysicsNeMo provides AI physics skills for training and deploying models, while CUDA-X libraries bring accelerated solvers and quantum chemistry capabilities into agentic engineering workflows. “Engineering has reached an inflection point. AI can now work with tools of physics, simulation and design,” said Timothy Costa, vice president and general manager of computational engineering at NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, developers can build agentic engineers that reason using physics, run complex simulations and generate high-fidelity data to become a new engine for innovation in chip and system design.” NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Adds AI Physics and Accelerated Computing Skills for Engineering AgentsNVIDIA Agent Toolkit helps developers build specialized engineering AI assistants connected to domain-specific tools, models and data. With the addition of NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and CUDA-X libraries, these agents can now use AI physics skills, accelerated solvers and quantum chemistry capabilities for chip, system and industrial engineering. Key capabilities include: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra Open Model Advances Agentic Coding for Chip DesignChip design depends on specialized register-transfer level (RTL) coding, which demands high accuracy, deep domain expertise and flexibility over deployment. With ACE-RTL — an agent for designing hardware from NVIDIA Research — NVIDIA Nemotron™ 3 Ultra leads among open models in agentic RTL coding on the comprehensive verilog design problems benchmark across RTL coding tasks. This represents how Nemotron 3 Ultra offers industry-leading accuracy and efficiency and can be post-trained on proprietary data — deployed locally or on premises — giving enterprises greater control, customization and data privacy as they build AI agents for chip design. Developers can get started with Nemotron 3 Ultra using Cadence’s harness; Synopsys’ fully autonomous, long-running agents for design verification and analog and mixed-signal workflows; Siemens’ Questa One smart verification agentic toolkit; as well as on Hugging Face. Software Leaders Build Autonomous AI Engineers With NVIDIAIndustrial engineering leaders are already using the new and expanded NVIDIA Agent Toolkit components to develop autonomous AI engineers. Cadence is using NVIDIA Nemotron, accelerated computing and CUDA-X libraries with the recently launched Cadence AuraStack AI Super Agent and the Cadence Millennium M2000 platform to autonomously drive advanced packaging and printed circuit board (PCB) design from exploration through signoff, delivering up to 20x faster multiphysics performance. This joins Cadence’s complete portfolio of silicon design super agents which collectively cover the chip design workflow end to end, from architecture through manufacturing signoff. In addition, the collaboration extends from agentic design to the underlying compute as Cadence’s portfolio of EDA and system design automation tools, including Cadence Jasper, a formal verification platform, is being optimized for the NVIDIA Vera CPU to help engineering teams validate advanced chip designs faster. Synopsys is using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA NIM™ microservices, Nemotron open models, the NVIDIA NeMo™ Gym library and NVIDIA NemoClaw™ blueprints with Synopsys AgentEngineer to build secure, accelerated agentic workflows across chip and system design. Leveraging Ansys Icepak, Synopsys’ agentic workflow autonomously executes simulation setup, and pre- and post-processing for complex GPU cooling design optimization. Synopsys is developing NVIDIA cuISS use cases to accelerate simulation workloads. The collaboration extends from agentic workflows to the underlying compute platform as Synopsys VCS, a high-performance functional verification solution used to simulate and validate complex chip designs before fabrication, is being optimized for the NVIDIA Vera CPU to help improve verification throughput. Siemens is using NVIDIA NeMo Gym, Nemotron open models and CUDA-X libraries with the Siemens Fuse EDA AI Agent to orchestrate multi-tool and multi-agent workflows across semiconductor, 3D-IC, PCB and system design, from conception through signoff. In Siemens Solido Characterization Suite, these agentic AI workflows are delivering more than 10x faster library characterization while reducing token costs by more than 10x. Samsung is using NVIDIA cuLitho and CUDA-X libraries to achieve up to 20x greater performance for computational lithography and applying NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo to perform chip-scale thermal-stress analysis with numerical solver-level accuracy across domains containing up to 10 billion cells. ChipAgents is using NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to build domain-specific AI agents for chip design and verification. The team is fine-tuning NVIDIA Nemotron models for complex end-to-end semiconductor design and verification workflows including debug, formal verification, coverage and more. Silvaco is using NVIDIA accelerated computing to scale high-accuracy 3D optical simulation in the Silvaco Victory Device. Running on 32 NVIDIA GPUs interconnected by NVIDIA NVLink™ technology, it completed a 3.2-billion-mesh-node photonic edge coupler simulation in under four hours, a workload beyond the practical limits of CPU-based simulation. Keysight is harnessing NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate electromagnetic simulations by up to 10x, while Samsung, Synopsys and TSMC are integrating NVIDIA cuEST into its GPU-accelerated pipeline to achieve up to a 50x speedup for key quantum-chemistry workloads. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at DAC. About NVIDIANVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI and accelerated computing. Title: Nvidia in Talks With OpenAI to Guarantee $250 Billion Financing for Data Center
URL: https://freerepublic.com/focus/f-chat/4389465/posts
Time Published: 2026-07-26T23:55:26Z
Full Content:
Skip to comments. Posted on 07/26/2026 4:55:26 PM PDT by E. Pluribus Unum Project would be one of the largest AI computing hubs and involve power controlled by the U.S. governmentNvidia NVDA is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI as part of a massive data center project, one of the most ambitious financial transactions yet in America’s artificial-intelligence boom.The guarantees from Nvidia would help the ChatGPT maker lease a 10-gigawatt project that SoftBank’s 9434 energy subsidiary is developing in southern Ohio, people familiar with the matter said. In total, the project could cost more than $500 billion, including the chips that would go inside the data centers. It would be the largest data center project announced to date.The power for the project is controlled by the U.S. government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is involved in deciding who will get the power, some of the people said.Nvidia’s backing would allow the data center developer, which is owned by Japanese billionaire Masayoshi Son’s investment firm SoftBank, to raise debt at more favorable terms than it could if OpenAI had no financial backer, since OpenAI has no investment-grade credit rating as an unprofitable private company. The AI company has been in advanced talks to lease the site for several weeks, people familiar with the matter said.OpenAI is among the companies that has shown most interest in the site, while Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also spoken to Lutnick about it in recent weeks, one of the people said. AI companies are desperate to secure chips and power needed to run their models, making megaprojects that have government support or guaranteed power increasingly attractive. Title: Tech Titans Slash 140K Jobs as AI Spending Soars
URL: https://www.pymnts.com/big-tech/2026/tech-titans-slash-140k-jobs-as-ai-spending-soars/
Time Published: 2026-07-26T23:10:46Z
Full Content:
American tech companies have cut close to 140,000 jobs this year amid record artificial intelligence spending. Complete the form to unlock this article and enjoy unlimited free access to all PYMNTS content — no additional logins required. yesSubscribe to our daily newsletter, PYMNTS Today. By completing this form, you agree to receive marketing communications from PYMNTS and to the sharing of your information with our sponsor, if applicable, in accordance with our Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions. Δ Those reductions account for more than a third of this year’s announced layoffs in the U.S., the Financial Times (FT) reported Sunday (July 26), citing its analysis of corporate filings and data from executive outplacement company Challenger, Gray and Christmas. Nearly 50,000 of those cuts came from Amazon, Oracle, Meta and Microsoft, the equivalent of around 6% of their total corporate workforce, the report said. These companies, along with Alphabet, are projected to spend well over $800 billion on AI-related efforts this year, FT added. As the FT noted, widespread layoffs have become de rigueur among Silicon Valley companies since the COVID pandemic hiring spree ended. Many of these firms have kept the cuts going while also investing heavily in AI infrastructure. The report added that the situation is in contrast with the health of the larger jobs market. Hiring has cooled since the post-pandemic surge, but government data shows America’s unemployment rate at a low 4.2%. FT also pointed to the mass layoffs earlier this year at Block, where CEO Jack Dorsey said AI was changing the company’s employment needs. However, the report added, some academics argue AI-related cuts give employers an excuse to remedy their mistakes. “The typical attitude of tech executives has been to say that AI allows us to gain efficiency rather than admit that they overhired,” said Enrico Moretti, a professor of economics at University of California, Berkeley. “It’s an easy way out.” At the same time, recent research from corporate card firm Ramp and workforce analytics firm Revelio Labs found that the companies spending the most on generative AI are expanding their staffing levels faster than the firms spending the least. “AI adopters saw headcount rise 10.2% over the two years following adoption, gains the study attributed entirely to high-intensity spenders,” PYMNTS wrote in a report on the findings. “Low-intensity adopters saw no statistically significant change in headcount over the same period. Within high-intensity adopters, the entry-level headcount grew 12%.” Meanwhile, some AI companies have begun walking back earlier predictions about AI-related job losses. For example, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said last year that AI could erase half of all entry-level roles, but has since taken on a more positive outlook. “They can do the same thing with less resources, and that leads to things like layoffs, or they can do more with the same amount of resources,” he said, per a report from The Wall Street Journal. “But that requires creativity.” Tech Titans Slash 140K Jobs as AI Spending Soars BitMart Becomes 2nd Crypto Exchange to Close in 3 Days EU's New MiCA Rules Could Mean More Crypto Mergers Card Delinquencies Creep Up as Consumers Rely More on Credit Get PYMNTS Today, AI, B2B and more. Title: South Korea's Naver jumps 10% on Nvidia's $1 billion investment plan
URL: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/south-koreas-naver-jumps-10-nvidias-1-billion-investment-plan-6279546
Time Published: 2026-07-26T23:04:39Z
Full Content:
East Asia FILE PHOTO: A general view of the Naver sign on its office building in Seongnam, South Korea, May 13, 2022. Picture taken May 13, 2022. REUTERS/ Heo Ran/File Photo SEOUL: Shares of South Korea's internet giant Naver jumped more than 10 per cent on Monday (Jul 27) after it said Nvidia would acquire US$1 billion of its new shares to finance a project to expand an AI data centre. The investment comes after the two firms and investment group Brookfield announced on Friday plans to expand Naver's AI data centre in South Korea with up to US$10 billion in funding. Naver said on Monday it will place 7.2 million new shares with Nvidia for 204,500 won each, or a 1 per cent discount to its closing price on Friday, as part of the agreement. Brookfield will provide up to US$9 billion in financing as the project's capital partner, Naver added. With the investment, Nvidia would become one of the biggest shareholders of Naver, owning a 4.5 per cent stake. The National Pension Service was the biggest shareholder of Naver with a 9.25 per cent stake, followed by BlackRock Fund Advisors with 6.12 per cent as of end-2025. The data centre will be built at Naver's GAK data centre in the city of Sejong in South Korea, using Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Blackwell chip platforms, and it will have a capacity of 200 megawatts by 2028. In June, Naver and Nvidia announced an agreement to jointly pursue the development of gigawatt-scale global AI infrastructure, aiming to tap demand for sovereign AI from the Asia-Pacific region, Europe and the Middle East. One gigawatt is about four times the maximum capacity of GAK Sejong, South Korea's largest hyperscale data centre operated by Naver. It represents a scale capable of accommodating hundreds of thousands of Nvidia's latest GPUs at once, Naver said. Title: BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Fidelity, and others back the Clarity Act with $30 trillion in combined firepower
URL: https://cryptobriefing.com/blackrock-goldman-fidelity-back-clarity-act/
Time Published: 2026-07-26T19:03:48Z
Full Content:
Searching... The biggest names in traditional finance are lining up behind crypto market structure legislation ahead of Congress's August recess Share A coalition of financial heavyweights managing north of $30 trillion in assets has thrown its weight behind the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, sending what might be the loudest signal yet that Wall Street wants crypto’s regulatory gray zone to end. BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Fidelity, Charles Schwab, and Grayscale are among the firms endorsing H.R. 3633, a bill designed to draw clear jurisdictional lines between the SEC and CFTC over digital assets. The timing is deliberate. Congress is barreling toward its August recess, and supporters of the legislation are applying pressure to keep the bill moving through the Senate Banking Committee before lawmakers scatter for the summer. The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, formally introduced on May 29, 2025, attempts to solve this by explicitly assigning oversight responsibilities between the two agencies. It also layers in anti-money laundering requirements, a concession that likely made the bill more palatable to regulators and lawmakers who’ve long worried about crypto’s use in illicit finance. Fidelity, which oversees approximately $7.1 trillion in assets, has been one of the most vocal supporters. The firm called on the Senate to pass the legislation, describing the framework as balanced and arguing it would bolster both investor confidence and US competitiveness in global digital asset markets. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon has also voiced support for the initiative, emphasizing the need for a structured market environment. The collective assets under management of the firms backing this bill exceed $30 trillion, with some estimates placing the combined figure closer to $50 trillion depending on how you count. Most of these firms have already dipped their toes into crypto. BlackRock launched its spot Bitcoin ETF in early 2024 and watched it become one of the most successful ETF launches in history. Fidelity has offered crypto custody and trading for years. But their engagement has been constrained, deliberately limited to the safest corners of the market because the regulatory picture has been so murky. The Senate Banking Committee’s movement on the bill suggests genuine legislative momentum. The FIT21 bill passed the House in 2024 with broad support and then languished in the Senate. Supporters of H.R. 3633 are clearly trying to avoid a repeat. Title: Kogan running 'clone' website selling same products at higher prices
URL: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-27/kogan-exclusive-brands-website-pricing/106891632
Time Published: 2026-07-26T18:59:25Z
Full Content:
Emergency Backstory Newsletters 中文新闻 BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA TOK PISIN Find any issues using dark mode? Please let us know Topic:Consumer Protection Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 4:59am Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 8:20am Kogan is operating a second website called Exclusive Brands, where it sells the same products at higher prices. (ABC News: Widia Jalal) An ABC investigation has discovered leading online retailer Kogan is operating a second website called Exclusive Brands, selling the same products with large price hikes. Experts, including a former ACCC boss, have called for the consumer watchdog to launch an urgent investigation into whether discounts on Kogan.com are misleading. Kogan has defended its use of the Exclusive Brands website and denied any wrongdoing. Leading online retailer Kogan is operating a second "clone" website to sell the same popular products at mostly higher prices, the ABC can reveal. The little-known website, called Exclusive Brands, has operated for years and sells Kogan's own brand products that include highly sought-after televisions, couches and washing machines, as well as furniture brands Matt Blatt and Brosa, bike and work-out range Fortis, and tool brand Certa. The revelation has led to calls for the retailer to be investigated over whether it's misleading customers by offering dubious discounts. There are concerns Kogan has unreasonably compared prices on Kogan.com to its secondary website, which appears not to have been heavily promoted. An ABC investigation discovered the prices charged on Exclusive Brands were usually much more than those charged on its flagship website kogan.com for the same products. The most expensive items were thousands of dollars more. Do you have a tip about how a company is treating consumers? Contact Michael Atkin on michaelatkin@protonmail.com or via the Signal secure messaging app +61 447 279 901. ABC analysis found that Kogan appeared to use the pricing differences to offer shoppers who were browsing kogan.com large discounts from what it calls the "standard retail price" (SRP). However, Kogan has denied this was solely based on the prices on the Exclusive Brands website, saying it also charged the higher prices on Kogan.com. "Kogan.com only advertises an SRP as a reference price where that price has been offered on kogan.com itself for a reasonable time and within a recent period of time," they said in a statement. "Standard Retail Pricing may also apply to the same product on other Kogan Group channels." The ABC uncovered large price differences between the two websites. (ABC News: Widia Jalal) When the ABC requested evidence of the higher prices being charged on Kogan.com in relation to four products cited in this story, the company declined but maintained it had done so. "Kogan Group does not disclose sales information regarding individual products," it said in a statement. The company said each of the items had recently been sold by Kogan.com at the SRP for a "reasonable period". According to experts, shoppers are highly motivated to buy a product if they perceive they are getting a bargain, and retailers are legally obliged to ensure the discounts are genuine. Former Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) boss Rod Sims said the revelations were of "great concern". Rod Sims is calling for the watchdog to investigate. (ABC News: Chris Taylor) Mr Sims questioned whether Kogan had used the Exclusive Brands site to make misleading price comparisons and called for the ACCC to launch an investigation. "If that Exclusive Brands website is not a real (price) comparator this would be extremely concerning, and I would have thought extremely important for the ACCC to investigate, because it matters to consumers," he said. Mr Sims said the public should not reach a conclusion until an investigation was complete. Kogan defended its use of the Exclusive Brands website and denied any wrongdoing. Kogan defended its use of the Exclusive Brands website. (ABC News: Che Chorley) The retailer said it was established to focus only on the company's exclusive products that it manufactures without any third-party products or marketplace items. Kogan was unavailable for interview, with a spokesperson saying in a statement its "price advertising and discount representation methodologies are carefully reviewed by independent external lawyers to ensure compliance with relevant laws". "We take our obligations to present pricing clearly and accurately very seriously." The retailer also said price differences between a brand's website and discount channels were common. Kogan was started 20 years ago by CEO Ruslan Kogan from his parents' garage. That modest start morphed into an ASX-listed company that has become a household name. The retailer, which currently boasts 3.5 million customers in Australia and New Zealand, took over Dick Smith and expanded into the telco, energy and insurance sectors. The Kogan website raked in more than $790 million in gross sales in the 2025 financial year alone, with its own branded products a major part of the business. Kogan's latest annual report said those brands "drove more than 70 per cent of sales within the Product Division, expanding margins and increasing the average value of items sold". But many shoppers may not have realised the large price difference for those products depends on what website they used. The ABC found a Brosa Palermo Sofa Bed to "transform your living space" selling for $3,999.99 on Exclusive Brands. The same sofa was being sold at a much higher price on Exclusive Brands than it was on Kogan.com. (Screenshot) However, on kogan.com, the same sofa was $1,229, with the website claiming a discount of more than $2,770 from the SRP. "This is the standard retail price at which this exclusive product is offered for sale by Kogan through one or more channels," a small disclaimer reads. A high-end 4K,100-inch Kogan television was sold on Exclusive Brands for $6,999.99. Exclusive Brands was selling the Kogan TV for thousands of dollars more than Kogan.com. (Screenshot) On the Kogan website, the price was $3,199 — a discount of almost $4,000. A Kogan washer/dryer with an 11kg/7kg capacity was selling for $1,699.99 on Exclusive Brands, compared to $739 on kogan.com, a discount of almost $1,000. The washer/dryer was almost $1000 cheaper on Kogan. (Screenshot) These prices were taken from the websites on July 15. The ABC analysed 1,033 products sold on Exclusive Brands and compared them to the prices charged for the same products on kogan.com. The analysis found the median price difference for a product between the sites was $100. The total price across all products analysed on the Exclusive Brands site was $393,895, while for kogan.com the total price was $220,610. Those products were sold for $173,285 more than the non-member price on Kogan.com and $193,553 more than a Kogan first member using kogan.com. Some products on kogan.com did not have an SRP comparison price. The prices analysed by the ABC were gathered on July 13 and 14. Mr Sims said the use of the Exclusive Brands website to create a higher comparison price with the lower price on kogan.com needed a "very close look" as companies could make a lot of money by making people feel like they were getting a bargain. "If that alternative website is not the normal way of transacting things, if it's just there to be there, then it could very well be misleading because you're not getting a bargain." Kogan did not answer specific questions about the price differences found by the ABC, saying it could not comment without being provided the "underlying product dataset or methodology". Kogan said it used "differentiated pricing and promotional calendars" across sales channels. Discounts from the SRP were made after properly establishing the higher price in accordance with the law, the spokesperson said. Tracey Villani purchased an air conditioner from Kogan last summer for a rental property she owns in Adelaide. She said the affordable price of $779 was a key factor and "quite a few hundred dollars below the recommended retail price". "I had compared prices with all the major retailers, other online places as well, and Kogan was the cheapest," she said. Tracey Villani purchased an air conditioner from Kogan, thinking it was heavily discounted. (ABC News: Che Chorley) The Kogan site indicated the product was being discounted from the SRP of the air conditioner, which was $1,300 on July 20, 2026. When Ms Villani had the appliance installed, it did not work. She requested a repair or a refund from Kogan, but she said they were "no help" so she arranged to have it fixed. When the ABC contacted the company about her experience, Kogan offered to repay the cost of repairing it and apologised for not resolving her issue sooner. When asked by the ABC if she had ever shopped on the Exclusive Brands website, Ms Villani said she had never heard of it. After browsing Exclusive Brands, she said she would not have any idea it was "actually a Kogan site". Tracey Villani did her research before buying the air conditioner and thought she was getting a good deal with Kogan. (ABC News: Che Chorley) Ms Villani said she thought she was getting a good deal. "You really need to do your research and see if their higher prices are actually a legitimate higher price and not one they've just invented to make their prices sound a lot cheaper." Ms Villani is not alone in her confusion about who owns and runs Exclusive Brands. On a shopping forum called OzBargain in April, there was a discussion about whether the site could be trusted after someone spotted a Kogan product being sold cheaply on Exclusive Brands. "I'm a bit concerned about whether exclusivebrands.com.au is legit or not… I can't find any history concerning the website. It seems really high effort to go to for a scam," one person wrote, A screenshot of the email sent by a Kogan.com customer service representative. (Supplied) The person wrote to Kogan and received confirmation it was "legitimate". "Exclusive Brands is used by Kogan to showcase and sell selected Kogan private-label and partner products through a dedicated storefront," the email response said. Former Kogan staff members familiar with the Exclusive Brands website spoke with the ABC on the condition of anonymity. One ex-staffer described it as a "clone" of the Kogan website with many of the same product listings, except with "prices marked up". They said some of the "astronomical" mark-ups felt "deceptive" and made them "uncomfortable". Multiple sources confirmed there were internal discussions several years ago about how Exclusive Brands was only used by a limited number of customers. The ACCC has raised a range of concerns about online retail marketplaces, such as Amazon Australia, Catch, eBay Australia and Kogan. Staff were surprised if customers purchased a product via Exclusive Brands and did not shop around, they said. The ABC searched Kogan's media releases and announcements to the Australian stock exchange but could not find any promotion or mention of the Exclusive Brands website. Kogan is a heavy advertiser with Google and Meta — which owns Facebook and Instagram — but their ad libraries also did not show any results for advertisements for Exclusive Brands. One former employee said they believed Kogan had paid to promote Exclusive Brands on Google but was unaware of other promotion of the site. The website also appeared to offer fewer payment options than kogan.com and did not offer the Kogan First membership discount pricing. However, former staff said there was an internal belief the company was using the Exclusive Brands website to show the value it was offering for its own-brand products and this was a legitimate loophole. Another ex-worker disagreed the use of the website was problematic, arguing it was a reasonable marketing strategy. When asked about how many shoppers used Exclusive Brands to buy products, Kogan said it did not "disclose its sales by channel". It did not answer a question about where it paid to advertise Exclusive Brands. "Kogan Group utilises paid advertising to support sales in all its channels, each of which contributes significantly to overall sales," the spokesperson said. Kogan has previously been in trouble over misleading discounts. The consumer watchdog won a Federal Court case in 2020 when Kogan was found to have misled shoppers during a tax-time sales promotion that spruiked a 10 per cent discount on more than 600 products if they entered a code. However, Kogan increased the price of the products immediately before the promotion and decreased the prices after the promotion finished. Jeannie Paterson, a consumer law expert from the University of Melbourne, said she was surprised to see such a big price difference between the two sites, and it was not clear the reason for it was occurring when they were both owned by Kogan. She said it was "really murky". Jeannie Paterson says the situation feels "murky". (ABC News: Patrick Stone) "Given there's such a significant price difference, why is that occurring? Is anybody actually buying products on the Exclusive Brands website or is it there simply to set a benchmark for the discount on the discount website?" Ms Paterson said customers would probably feel "misled" and "manipulated" after learning about the links between Exclusive Brands and Kogan. She agreed an ACCC investigation was needed into whether Kogan was exploiting a legal loophole or if a court might find it was illegally misleading consumers. "It would be within the capacity of the ACCC to ask some of these questions about whether there's any marketing budget spent on Exclusive Brands, what the level of sales are and what the foot traffic is or the online traffic is." Shares in online retailer Kogan tumble after the Federal Court finds its "tax time: promotion was misleading but the ASX 200 finishes higher after a choppy session. Mr Sims said an investigation should also probe Kogan about why the Exclusive Brands website was set up, what each product's normal price was and whether it was set by Exclusive Brands or not. If the normal price was set by Exclusive Brands but few people used it, that could be a problem for Kogan, he said. Kogan denied that it was misleading customers. "Kogan's pricing principles comply with all applicable laws and regulations and are supported by strict internal governance and compliance processes." The ACCC refused to comment on whether it would investigate. In a statement, it said consumer law prevented businesses from "making false or misleading statements about prices, including about savings and discounts". "This is important to ensure both that consumers can make informed purchasing decisions, and that businesses who are doing the right thing are not unfairly disadvantaged. "Stating that the sale price is marked down from an earlier price can be misleading when the items were not offered for sale at the price for a reasonable period right before the sale started, or only a very small proportion of the items sold at that price right before the sale." "It can also be misleading to compare the displayed price to a recommended retail price (RRP) that the product was never sold at, or was not sold at for a reasonable period right before the sale started." Title: Former minister for children calls for pause on planned development at Bessborough
URL: https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/2026/07/26/former-minister-for-children-calls-for-pause-on-planned-development-at-bessborough/
Time Published: 2026-07-26T18:23:43Z
Full Content:
Former minister for children Katherine Zappone has called for a pause on a controversial planned development at the site of a former mother and baby home. Earlier this year Estuary View Enterprises was granted planning permission by Cork City Council to build 140 apartments on the grounds of Bessborough in Blackrock on the southside of Cork city. Bessborough Mother and Baby Home Support Group and Cllr Peter Horgan of Labour lodged appeals to An Coimisiún Pleanála. On July 9th the commission upheld permission for the building of 108 apartments on the site. This caused dismay among survivors of the home who are vehemently opposed to the development. The Commission of Investigation into Mother and Baby Homes estimated that 923 babies died at the home between the 1920s and 1990s. The burial place of more than 859 children remains unknown. In an interview with RTÉ’s This Week programme Zappone said significant efforts should be made to determine the scale of burial at Bessborough. “I think this can and should be done now before development. I think there should be a pause now in relation to the development. [ Former minister Zappone raised concerns about building apartments on Bessborough siteOpens in new window ] “The careful, honest and moral thing to do is to look properly before we build. “Why would the State not want to do something about this? “We know 859 [children] and 19 mothers died at Bessborough and they have no known grave.” The former minister believes a geophysical survey ought to be carried out at Bessborough. “We need to have a similar approach to Bessborough as we did in Tuam, it needs to be taken one step at a time and to determine how to do that. “The primary concerns, as I hear it, and as our special advocate Patricia Carey talks about, they [the victims and survivors] have the right to know where their loved ones are buried and that’s what I am arguing for.” [ State urged to buy former Bessborough mother and baby home lands to create memorial parkOpens in new window ] Zappone said what was done in Tuam “wasn’t done in Bessborough”. She indicated that when she was minister for children she received the burial reports from the commission of investigation. “In that report they identified that there were modest efforts to ascertain the location and the scale of the burial at Bessborough. “Forensic archaeologists basically assessed the visible landscape but determined that there were no visible features that indicated that there was something or that human remains may be buried underneath.” Zappone insisted this wasn’t “sufficient” nor was it comparable to what occurred at Tuam. Meanwhile, in a letter of appeal to the commission earlier this year Zappone expressed her belief in the “human dignity” of the mothers and children associated with Bessborough whose burial places are not known. However, in its decision to uphold planning permission the commission stated there was no evidence of unrecorded burials in the area where the development is proposed. Conditions attached to the planning permission include forensic archaeological monitoring during construction work and the appointment of a liaison officer to engage with survivor groups. Title: You Langer: Colette Sheridan on a wonderful new book of Cork’s slang words
URL: https://www.irishtimes.com/opinion/an-irish-diary/2026/07/26/you-langer-colette-sheridan-on-a-wonderful-new-book-of-corks-slang-words/
Time Published: 2026-07-26T18:00:00Z
Full Content:
A self-described blow-in from Mayo who has only been living in Cork for more than 50 years, Des MacHale, author of joke books and emeritus professor of mathematics at University College Cork, recently had his latest book launched at the Kerryman’s bar, Cork. Langers & Lashes: A Compendium of Cork Slang claims to be the most comprehensive collection of Cork slang published. The title describes utter fools or arrogant types and attractive women. (“Langer” is also a Cork word for the male appendage and its plural form refers to someone wasted from drink.) Singer Tim O’Riordan belted out verses of his irreverent ballad, The Langer Song, at the launch. It was followed by a couple of words from MacHale’s son Dominic – an actor best known for playing Garda Sergeant Healy in the TV series The Young Offenders. (Dominic MacHale and fellow actor Shane Casey, who plays Billy Murphy in the Cork northside-based comedy, were taking time off from watching the World Cup for their humorous take on the games for RTÉ 2.) As the author’s son said, it takes an outsider to identify the slang that trips off the tongues of the natives. The book is certainly comprehensive with the inclusion of some slang that this writer never heard of despite being a Corkonian – albeit from the southside. That north/south dichotomy is important in Cork. “Norries” living north of the river Lee are generally seen as salt of the earth (think Roy Keane), unlike the “Sorries” who have notions, such as the fictional social media “Reggie” character living in a mansion on the salubrious Blackrock Road. (As it happens, Des MacHale is a resident of Blackrock.) This suburb would not be a hotbed of Cork slang. Which is why MacHale is indebted to members of the Frank O’Connor Book Club in Mayfield and the Blackpool Library Creative Writing Circle on the north side for their valuable contributions to the book. MacHale writes that most of the slang words in his book are words he has heard used in Cork over the years or words that have been reported to him as being in use. Apart from its religious connotation, I’ve never heard of the other meaning of “immaculate conception”, which refers to someone who develops a drink problem without ever standing a round. This phrase was imparted to MacHale by the late humorist, Niall Tóibín. Some of the slang in the book is “potentially offensive”, but rather than being censorious the dictionary preserves, in the interests of their historical contexts, words that embody prejudices that society now rejects. Crude anatomical and sexual references are included in the book to reflect the vernacular of old. Women come in for a disproportionate amount of derogatory terms, judging their behaviour, appearance and sexuality, compared to men. A difficult woman is “a wagon” while a good-looking female is a “fine half” or a “flah”. The latter word is also used as a verb for sexual congress. These terms are familiar to Corkonians, but how often is a word such as “balubas” used? To be balubas is to be seriously drunk. The term originated when Cork soldiers serving in the United Nations peacekeeping forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (1960-1964) “inappropriately adopted the name of the Baluba people as slang. While still in use, using an African people’s name in this derogatory way reflects colonial-era attitudes that are recognised as offensive today”. Hardly offensive, though, except to particularly uptight parents, is the term “electrocution lessons” to help a child modify their accent and speech patterns. As a kid, I was sent to elocution classes (we never used the word electrocution in that jokey way) to try to nullify my burgeoning Cork accent. Southside mothers had antennae for picking up that sing/song way of speaking that wouldn’t help one’s career prospects on South Mall. Coming home from playing on the streets, an unsuspecting kid might ask for a glass of raza (raspberry cordial). The only response was to call in reinforcements, which involved packing him/her off to elocution sessions. Do people still send their kids to elocution? Or would that be considered too elitist these days? Still, the slang phrase “he spoke very well dressed” describes someone with a “superior accent or method of speaking”. I haven’t come across it, but it is in keeping with the Cork sense of humour, mixing and matching unlikely concepts so they make a certain kind of sense. In a note from the publisher, Mercier, the book is described as intending to be a scholarly reference on the development of Cork vernacular and not as a guide for contemporary usage. But we still hang on to such gems as “getting a fifty”, which sums up being ghosted when only 50 per cent turns up for a date. Cork slang is, of course, superior to that of any other slang in the country. Admittedly, we natives are guilty of Cork exceptionalism – which perhaps merits a book all of its own. © 2026 The Irish Times DAC
